title: Wendy’s joins Sri Lanka’s fast-food race through JKH - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - John Keells Holdings PLC (JKH) will bring the global fast-food chain Wendy’s to Sri Lanka, marking the diversified conglomerate’s entry into the quick-service restaurant segment.

The first Wendy’s outlet is expected to open by December 2026, with the franchise agreements and other preliminary work already completed.

“JKH will diversify its consumer foods portfolio into Sri Lanka’s quick service restaurant segment through the rollout of the internationally recognised Wendy’s brand,” JKH Chairperson Krishan Balendra said in the group’s latest quarterly release.

JKH is yet to disclose the location of the first outlet, the investment involved or the number of restaurants planned under the rollout.

The group’s consumer foods segment reported earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of Rs.1.52 billion for the quarter ended June 2026, up 21 percent, from Rs.1.26 billion a year earlier.

The segment’s performance was supported by a strong volume growth, with the beverage volumes rising 27 percent and confectionery volumes increasing 13 percent during the quarter.

title: Unidentified object lands deep inside Poland causing explosion as Russia launches deadly, Ukraine-wide attack - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
CNN - An unidentified object crashed and caused an explosion about 90 kilometers (55 miles) into Polish territory early Thursday, local authorities said, as Russia launched deadly longe-range attacks across Ukraine.

Poland had earlier reported scrambling fighter jets in response to Russia’s attack on Ukraine, which hit large swathes of the country and killed at least eight people, including children, and left several people trapped under rubble.

The object crashed in an undeveloped area near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia in Lublin province, Poland’s army said. Polish police said residents reported hearing a powerful blast.

“During the Russian massive missile attack on western Ukraine, a violation of Polish airspace occurred,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said in a post to X. A government spokesperson said Tusk was on his way to the crash site.

Separately, Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said a Russian cruise missile had “crossed into Poland as part of Russia’s massive strike against Ukraine” in a post to X. It was not clear if Sybiha was referring to the unidentified object which crashed in Lublin.

Russia’s Ministry of Defense said it carried out a “massive strike using long-range precision weapons from land, air, and sea” as well as attack drones on military sites across Ukraine, in a statement posted to Telegram Thursday.

Poland’s army said the country’s air defenses observed at least a dozen missiles over western Ukraine, which posed a potential threat to Polish airspace.

It is not yet clear if the unidentified object that crashed in Poland was a Russian missile. But any potential Russian attack so deep into a NATO member’s territory would risk being perceived as an escalation in Moscow’s yearslong war on Ukraine.

CNN has reached out to NATO for comment.

Russia’s overnight assault on Ukraine follows a visit by President Volodymyr Zelensky to the White House Tuesday, where he asked President Donald Trump to provide Ukraine with additional air defense systems.

The attack damaged or destroyed dozens of homes, businesses and infrastructure facilities, Zelensky said on Telegram Thursday, and used more than 70 missiles and over 280 attack drones.

Ukraine intercepted more than 260 drones, according to Zelensky, in what he said was a commendable feat given a “critical shortage of air defense missiles from our partners.”

On his way home on Wednesday, Zelensky stopped in the Polish city of Lublin – not far from the site of the next day’s crash – to meet with Tusk. The two leaders discussed “the outcomes of (Zelensky’s) visit to the United States and the security of Poland, Ukraine, and all of Europe,” according to a post to X by Tusk.

Poland has routinely scrambled jets in response to Russian attacks on western Ukraine, though they have rarely entered its territory. NATO fighter jets shot down multiple Russian drones that violated Polish airspace last September, denouncing Moscow for “absolutely dangerous behavior.”

In November 2022, two people were killed after a Ukrainian air defense missile unintentionally landed in the Polish village of Przewodow, about four miles (6.4 kilometers) west of the border.

The attacks – which come as Ukraine has seen its heaviest number of civilian casualties in one month since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022 – killed at least one person in the capital Kyiv, and another person in Poltava region, central Ukraine, according to local authorities.

Videos posted on social media showed families sheltering in crowded Kyiv metro stations, some bedding down on the floor beneath blankets or inside small tents.

In the village of Radushne, near the southern Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, parents and three children were killed after a ballistic missile blew a family home “into smithereens,” Zelensky said. Two more children were pulled alive from the rubble, he added.

Two girls, aged 5 and 12, were among the three children killed, Oleksandr Vilkul, head of the city’s military administration, said on Telegram, calling it a “dark night.”

Graphic video from Radushne showed bodies strewn amid the rubble of a shattered building, with fires still burning.

Two unseen women could be heard speaking. “We’ve pulled one child out. There are still some lying over there,” one said.

“There are children here. There are many children,” the other said.

Rescue workers were also trying to save people trapped under rubble after an attack on a residential building in Lviv, Zelensky said. Dozens across the country were wounded.

Also on Thursday, a warehouse for the Russian retailer Wildberries caught fire in the western city of Penza after a Ukrainian drone attack, regional governor Oleg Melnichenko said on Telegram. One person was wounded and about 200 people were evacuated from the site, Melnichenko said.

Ukraine has repeatedly targeted Wildberries distribution centers, Russia’s Amazon equivalent, bringing Moscow’s war even closer to home by disrupting the lives and livelihoods of ordinary Russians.

Kyiv has claimed the Wildberries facilities are legitimate military targets because they supply Russia’s frontline troops in Ukraine, which Moscow denies.

title: Sri Lanka-US diplomatic ties stronger than ever: Mahinda Samarasinghe - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Sisira Wijesinghe from Washington DC

July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka's Ambassador to the United States, Mahinda Samarasinghe, said diplomatic cooperation between Sri Lanka and the United States has grown stronger than ever during his tenure, resulting in significant progress in the country's economic development.

He made the remarks during a visit to the Maryland International Buddhist Temple on July 28, where he received blessings from the Chief Judicial Sanghanayake of the United States, Most Venerable Katugastota Uparathana Nayaka Thero.

Addressing the gathering, Ambassador Samarasinghe said the United States now holds a very positive perception of Sri Lanka and has extended assistance in several areas supporting the country's economic development.

He highlighted the importance of maintaining and further strengthening the longstanding cooperation between the two countries.

Speaking at the event, Ven. Katugastota Uparathana Nayaka Thero praised Ambassador Samarasinghe's service, saying his contribution to Sri Lanka had gone beyond the traditional role of a diplomat.

The Thero further said that a stronger and more optimistic bridge had been built between Sri Lanka and the United States than ever before, adding that Ambassador Samarasinghe had played a leading role in fostering those ties.

title: Uefa to hold emergency meeting over Fifa World Cup plans - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.30 - Uefa will hold an emergency meeting on Thursday afternoon to discuss its response to the controversial World Cup stakeholder plans proposed by Fifa and its president Gianni Infantino.

European football's governing body kept up its offensive over the plans after it was discovered Fifa had sent a letter, seen by the BBC, to all 211 member associations giving them until 19 September to decide if they want to accept the deal, and with it the first $20m (£15m) of an initial $40m (£30m).

"We have learned of Fifa's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn," said Uefa. "This says everything you need to know about this plan."

It was Uefa's second statement on the issue. The first claimed Fifa had "crossed a line".

It is not known precisely what will be discussed at the meeting, which will be held virtually.

Many associations, including the Football Association, are furious at only learning through the media of the proposal to sell a 20% stake in Fifa competitions to private finance - led by the Thrive Eternal investment vehicle owned by Joshua Kushner, the brother-in-law of US President Donald Trump's daughter Ivanka.

FA chairwoman Debbie Hewitt was among the Fifa vice-presidents not given advance warning. Uefa's unease has been echoed by the Asian, South American and North and Central American Confederations.

Former FA and Manchester City chairman David Bernstein said England must "withdraw" from the World Cup if Infantino's proposals go through.

Three of the 2026 World Cup semi-finalists are among Uefa's 55 members. It knows the nuclear option of its members pulling out of the tournament would severely damage the financial viability of the concept.

That is very much viewed as the outer edge of what is possible, particularly as one Uefa member has said it is broadly in agreement with Infantino's proposals.

"We can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football," said Czech Republic FA president David Trunda.

Fifa's explanation for controversial move

After widespread condemnation of both the proposals and the manner in which they have been created, Fifa released an eight-page document highlighting the reasons behind them on Wednesday evening.

Fifa said its view was that "too little of football's growing commercial value has reached the parts of the game that need it most".

It has been pointed out the sums being spoken about are more than some member associations spend annually and questions have been raised about the auditing of money Fifa already hands over in some parts of the world.

Despite this, Infantino feels the proposals would help provide funding for "better pitches, stronger national teams, more pathways for young players, and greater support for women's football".

In a video released by Fifa on Wednesday, Infantino defended the plans, calling them "an offer, not an obligation".

"It's part of a democratic process - a consultation process - and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation," he added.

"It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally."

Fifa points to the qualification of Cape Verde, Curacao, Jordan and Uzbekistan for the World Cup for the first time as an example of the positive benefits of its work, although that was, in part, due to the expansion of the competition to 48 teams.

Fifa also cites Formula 1, La Liga, Ligue 1 and the Bundesliga as examples of other sporting organisations that use "dedicated commercial operations".

It says private investors would "absolutely not" have any influence over the World Cup.

What has the reaction been?

Wednesday saw a stream of comment on the issue, most of it negative.

The European Leagues organisation said Fifa's proposals represented "a reckless and divisive development for world football".

"The World Cup should not be for sale. It is not the Fifa president's private equity asset," a statement read.

Global players' union Fifpro called on Fifa to "reconsider its proposal without further delay".

It said it had "noted with deep concern the proposal to transform the World Cup and other Fifa competitions into investable assets for private capital".

Fifpro added that such a move "would fundamentally and irreversibly reshape the incentives underpinning the competitions" and it was "particularly troubling that a project of this magnitude has been developed largely behind closed doors".

La Liga president Javier Tebas accused Infantino of trying to buy votes before the next Fifa congress in March.

"It doesn't seem like a reform. It seems like an electoral campaign financed with the future of football," Tebas said.

"Development cannot be used to buy votes or silences. The competitions and commercial rights of Fifa are not the personal patrimony of Infantino.

"Whoever mixes politics, discipline, money and power without transparency cannot lead anything.

"Infantino is not the solution to Fifa's governance. He is the problem."

Hans-Joachim Watzke, current vice-president of the German Football Association (DFB) and president of Borussia Dortmund, told Kicker magazine that Fifa's plans are an "absolute attack on football".

He said: "A line has been crossed here. If European football stands united against these plans, that carries a great deal of weight." - BBC

title: Dengue cases surpass 84,000 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Poojathmi Rivithma

Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka has recorded 84,091 dengue cases so far this year, with the dengue-related death toll reaching 61, according to the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU).

The NDCU said the highest number of dengue cases has been recorded from the Gampaha, Colombo, Kandy, Matara, Kalutara, and Galle districts.

In July alone, 28,717 dengue cases have been reported to date, highlighting a significant rise in infections.

Meanwhile, the NDCU said 175 high-risk dengue zones remain across the country.

Authorities have urged the public to keep their homes and surroundings clean to prevent mosquito breeding.

The NDCU also advised those experiencing fever to avoid taking medication other than paracetamol and to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms persist or worsen.

title: Rahane calls time on cricket - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.30 (Mirror Sports) - Ajinkya Rahane has announced his retirement from all forms of cricket, bringing the curtain down on a remarkable career. The elegant right-hander represented India in 195 international matches across all formats, leaving behind a legacy of resilience, leadership and memorable performances, particularly in Test cricket.

Rahane enjoyed his greatest success in the longest format, scoring 5,077 runs in 85 Tests, including 12 centuries. He also captained India to a historic Border-Gavaskar Trophy series victory in Australia in 2020-21, one of the country's greatest Test triumphs.

The 37-year-old also played 90 One-Day Internationals and 20 Twenty20 Internationals, contributing to India's run to the semi-finals of the 2015 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup. His retirement marks the end of a distinguished career built on composure, consistency and leadership.

title: Minister assures uninterrupted water supply for next three months - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - There is no need for water cuts at present as the Labugama and Kalatuwawa reservoirs hold enough water to meet demand for the next three months, Housing, Construction and Water Supply Minister Susil Ranasinghe said.

The Minister said that although weather forecasts indicate below-average rainfall in August and September due to the El Niño phenomenon, assessments carried out by experts of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) have confirmed that existing water storage levels are adequate to maintain a continuous water supply.

However, the Minister cautioned that the situation could change depending on future weather conditions and rainfall patterns.

title: Australia sues Telegram over failure to remove terrorist content - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BNO NEWS - Australia’s online safety regulator has sued Telegram, alleging that the messaging platform failed to detect and remove terrorist executions, mass shootings and other unlawful material.

The eSafety Commissioner filed civil penalty proceedings in Federal Court on Wednesday following a year-long investigation. Telegram could face penalties of up to 54.6 million Australian dollars (about 38 million USD) if the court finds that it violated the country’s online safety laws.

The regulator alleges that publicly posted videos of terrorist executions remained accessible for up to three weeks after Australian users reported them to Telegram.

Videos of the 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings in New Zealand and the 2022 Buffalo supermarket shooting in New York were also uploaded to Telegram and remained available for nearly three months before being removed, according to the regulator.

Telegram is further accused of failing to remove accounts, channels and groups that distributed unlawful material, allowing the content to be uploaded again. The company also allegedly failed to effectively deter its distribution or inform users about the outcome of their complaints.

The regulator said Telegram’s terms of service did not prohibit users from accessing or distributing pro-terror material across all parts of the platform.

“This case concerns content linked to some of the most notorious acts of known extremist violence in recent history,” eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant said. “We allege that this content remained accessible on the service long after Telegram had been put on notice.”

Inman Grant said the spread of extremist content risks normalizing violence and facilitating the recruitment and radicalization of vulnerable people. She noted that Telegram has more than 1 billion users worldwide and is visited by Australians an average of 1.5 million times each month.

Australian law requires online services to take steps to prevent, detect, deter and disrupt unlawful material, including child sexual abuse content, terrorist propaganda and extreme violence. The regulator is asking the court to impose a financial penalty and issue other orders against Telegram.

title: Ranil visits Bhutan - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe is currently in Bhutan on a private visit, a spokesman from his office said today.

Wickremesinghe left for Bhutan on Monday and is expected to return on Sunday, August 2, 2026.

title: Two killed after cab crashes against tree in Vavuniya - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Two persons were killed after a cab transporting vegetables crashed against a tree in the Kanagarayankulam area along the Jaffna–Kandy main road in Vavuniya early today, police said.

Police said the accident occurred when the cab, which was travelling from Dambulla to Jaffna carrying a load of vegetables, veered off the road and collided against a roadside tree.

Preliminary investigations suggest that the driver may have fallen asleep at the wheel, causing the vehicle to lose control.

The injured victims were admitted to the Mankulam Hospital, where they later succumbed to their injuries.

The bodies have been transferred to the Vavuniya Hospital mortuary, where post-mortem examinations are scheduled to be conducted.

Kanagarayankulam Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.

title: Singapore fines French teen $465 for viral straw-licking stunt - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - A Singapore court has fined a French student S$600 ($465; £348) for licking a straw from an orange juice vending machine and putting it back into its dispenser.

Didier Gaspard Owen Maximilien, 19, pleaded guilty to one count of public nuisance.

Maximilien, who is studying in Singapore, posted the video of himself licking the straw on Instagram with the caption "city is not safe".

Many online reacted with disgust to his video, which was reposted on a community page and picked up by local news outlets.

The company that owns the vending machine, iJooz, said it replaced all 500 straws in the machine dispenser after Maximilien's stunt.

Public nuisance offenders in Singapore face up to a S$2,000 fine, three months in jail, or both.

Both the prosecution and the defence sought a fine for Maximilien.

Maximilien is "truly sorry for having caused all this trouble and he realises that what appeared to him at that time as something perhaps playful has turned out to be something very consequential," a defence lawyer was quoted as saying by The Straits Times.

Serving freshly-squeezed orange juice at S$2 per cup, iJooz vending machines are a common sight in shopping districts, train stations and housing blocks in Singapore.

Maximilien licked the straw from an iJooz machine in Goldhill Centre on 12 March, in one of the city-state's more affluent neighbourhoods, after a boxing workout, Channel News Asia reported.

title: Red warning issued for strong winds, rough seas - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - The Department of Meteorology has issued a red warning for strong winds and rough seas off the coasts extending from Kankesanthurai to Kalpitiya via Mannar and from Hambantota to Pottuvil.

The Department said the sea areas off the coasts extending from Kankesanthurai to Kalpitiya via Mannar and from Hambantota to Pottuvil will be very rough at times with strong gusty winds up to 60 to 70 kmph.

Naval and fishing communities have been advised not to venture into these sea areas until further notice.

The sea areas off the coasts extending from Trincomalee to Kankesanthurai via Mullaittivu and Kalpitiya to Hambantota via Colombo and Galle will be rough at times with strong gusty winds up to 50 to 60 kmph.

The wave height is expected to increase about 2.0 to 2.5 metres in the sea areas off the coast extending from Mannar to Pottuvil via Colombo, Galle and Hambantota.

Meanwhile,the Meteorology Department said strong winds of about (40-50) kmph can be expected at times over Northern, North-central, North-western and Central provinces and in Rathnapura, Monaragala, Hambantota and Trincomalee districts due to the active south-west monsoonal condition.

title: Sri Lanka collects over 43 containers of plastic pellets from MSC Elsa 3 spill - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - The Marine Environment Protection Authority (MEPA) said that more than 43 containers worth of plastic pellets which washed ashore following the sinking of the MSC Elsa 3 vessel off the Kerala coast had been collected so far.

MEPA Chairman Samantha Gunasekara said the plastic pellets continue to wash ashore along the coastline from the Jaffna islands to Galle, with the situation worsening due to the monsoon season.

He said that around 1,800 workers have been deployed for the removal of the plastic pellets, with the costs being covered by the relevant shipping company.

Meanwhile, preparations are underway to estimate the compensation required for the damage caused to Sri Lanka’s marine ecosystem due to the sinking of the vessel. The expert committee appointed for this purpose also held a meeting yesterday, the chairman said.

The Liberian-flagged container ship MSC Elsa 3 sank on May 25, 2025, after developing a water leak in waters located about 38 nautical miles off the coast of Kerala, India. The vessel was carrying 643 containers at the time of the incident.

title: Don’t put judges in a difficult position: Opposition MP - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - While noting that a time will come when judges in Sri Lanka will have to deliver a judgement on themselves, Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekera yesterday said they would be called upon to make a determination on a proposal to extend their retirement age by two years, a decision that would benefit them.

"The government should not put the judges into a difficult situation by making them give a determination which will benefit them," the MP told journalists.

He also said the President should hold a referendum to seek the views of the people on the matter.

"A referendum should be called for to seek the view of the people because the retirement age of judges is a constitutional amendment. President Anura Kumara Dissanayake should therefore call a referendum as it was done by late President J. R. Jayewardene," he said.

Asked about the allegation by government members that the opposition is disturbed because legal cases are to be filed against some politicians, including the Rajapaksa's, Jayasekera said the government could file cases against anyone but should not interfere with the judiciary.

title: Wild Elephants push down garden wall to eat jak - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Kanchana Kumara

Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Three wild elephants which had entered Sigiriya town in the early hours of last morning had pushed down a parapet wall of a home garden to eat jak fruit from a tree.

The owner said a herd of three wild elephants had entered the garden at about 3.30am after pushing down the 200ft long garden wall and eaten jak fruits.

They said they informed the wildlife officers on the incident but to no avail. They pointed out that their house is in close proximity to the Wildlife Department office, but they came out with the excused that they were not in a position to visit the scene for want of a vehicle.

Residents of Sigriya area said they have been facing the threat of wild elephants since long and that they are living in constant fear. They pointed out that groups of tourists visiting Sigiriya area and frequenting the roads during day and night are at the mercy of the marauding jumbos.
